report:
**Conclusion: Yes — honey likely helps reduce acute cough symptoms in children over one year of age, though the evidence quality is low to moderate.**

**Evidence supporting honey:**

A 2023 systematic review (European Journal of Pediatrics) concluded that honey seems more effective than placebo/no treatment or cough medications in relieving acute cough symptoms in children, though evidence quality was ranked very low to low ([Springer](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00431-023-05066-1); [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/)).

The 2018 Cochrane Review found **moderate-certainty evidence** that honey probably reduces cough frequency better than no treatment or placebo, and relieved cough sooner than salbutamol. It also found low-quality evidence that honey may be slightly better than diphenhydramine ([Cochrane Library](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full); [Cochrane summary](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children)).

The American Academy of Family Physicians states honey can reduce cough frequency and severity and improve sleep for both children and parents compared with placebo or no treatment ([AAFP](https://www.aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2016/0701/p20.html)).

The Mayo Clinic notes honey may help calm coughs in adults and children over one year of age ([Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/symptoms/cough/expert-answers/honey/faq-20058031)).

**Caveats and counterpoints:**

- Evidence quality is generally low; trials are small and heterogeneous, and better-designed RCTs are needed.
- An earlier Cochrane review (2014) found "no strong evidence for or against" honey ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25404607/)).
- **Honey must never be given to infants under 12 months** due to the risk of infant botulism from *Clostridium botulinum* spores ([Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/infant-botulism); [KidsHealth](https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/honey-botulism.html)).

**Bottom line:** For children over one year, honey is a reasonable, low-risk option that modestly reduces cough frequency and improves sleep, but the evidence base remains limited.
